channel.title: Hastings Daily
channel.description: Local news for Hastings and St Leonards, three times a day.

item.title: Hastings Old Town landmark property goes to auction
item.description: A mixed commercial and residential property in Hastings Old Town is coming up for auction in December. The end-terrace at 58A & 58B High Street is listed with a freehold guide price of £260,000-plus. It is famously known as the Shirley Leaf & Petal Company and home to the Flower Makers Museum.

item.title: Quiz night raises £983 for Hastings RNLI lifeboat crew
item.description: Hastings RNLI has raised £983 to support its lifeboat crew following a quiz night held on Sunday, November 22. The event took place at the East Hastings Sea Angling Association.

item.title: Hastings pub wins platinum grading in Loo of the Year Awards
item.description: The John Logie Baird pub in Havelock Road, Hastings, has been awarded a platinum grading in the Loo of the Year Awards 2026. The accolade recognises the quality and standards of the facility's toilets, which were judged by inspectors during unannounced visits.

item.title: Hastings care home residents to be re-housed after funding dispute
item.description: East Sussex County Council is working to find new accommodation for 28 residents of Old Hastings House after failing to agree on increased placement costs.

item.title: New youth hub opens at 6-7 Cornwallis Street in Hastings
item.description: A new youth hub has opened at 6-7 Cornwallis Street in Hastings. The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) said the facility is open Monday to Friday and is part of a government plan to deliver a youth hub in every area of the UK.

item.title: Hastings United boss Ronnie Dolan confident of turnaround after slump
item.description: Hastings United manager Ronnie Dolan says the team will "start firing again" as they look to end a slump that has seen them lose five Isthmian League East games in six.

item.title: East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust asks visitors to wear masks amid respiratory rise
item.description: East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust has asked people to wear face masks in some areas of its hospitals.

item.title: New bid to sell alcohol at Hastings convenience store
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is considering a new application to sell alcohol from a convenience store in the town centre. The premises, located at 5 to 6 Harold Place, is currently occupied by Forever Food. The latest bid, submitted by Subash Yogarajah, seeks permission for off-sales of alcohol from 10am to 11pm, seven days a week. The application also indicates plans to rename the business Harold Express.

item.title: Hastings & Bexhill Harriers launch free Monday evening women's run
item.description: Hastings & Bexhill Harriers have introduced a new Monday evening initiative for women across the local community. The group aims to create a welcoming environment where participants can enjoy running in company, build confidence and feel safer.

item.title: Separating fact from fiction? A debate over Gareth Jones' famine reporting
item.description: A debate has emerged in the Hastings Online Times over the interpretation of journalist Gareth Jones' 1933 reporting on the Soviet famine.

item.title: Energy price cap rises to £2,166 for typical households
item.description: Ofgem has announced that the energy price cap will rise to £2,166 for a typical dual-fuel household paying by direct debit from 1 January to 31 March 2027. The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero, Ms Polly Billington, stated in the Commons that this increase is driven primarily by soaring international wholesale gas prices resulting from the war in Iran.

item.title: Drawing Life carers exhibition opens at Electro Studios
item.description: Drawing Life, run by Judy Parkinson, is hosting a Christmas exhibition at Electro Studios in St Leonards on 4, 5 and 6 December. The show features artworks created this year by unpaid carers and the people they care for.

item.title: Hastings Pride in Place board agrees £75,000 capacity funding
item.description: The Hastings Pride in Place Board met on 13 November to decide how to allocate capacity funding for community groups. The board agreed to release up to £75,000 for the current funding round, with the remaining £25,000 from the total £100,000 allocation carried forward to future rounds.

item.title: Line-side fault causes incorrect train delays on Hastings-Ashford route
item.description: Trains between Hastings and Ashford International are showing as delayed on journey planners this morning, Wednesday 25 November, due to a line-side equipment fault.

item.title: Ombudsman upholds complaint against East Sussex County Council
item.description: The Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman has upheld a complaint against East Sussex County Council regarding the handling of a child’s special educational needs.

item.title: On this day, 1846: Hastings line opens in stages from the north
item.description: This week in 1846, the Hastings line of the South Eastern Railway opened in stages from the north, with the first section commencing on 25 November. The line was later extended from Robertsbridge to Battle on 18 January 1852. It served as a terminus for only a month before the line was completed to Bopeep Junction on 18 February 1852.

item.title: Snow White panto returns to The White Rock this Christmas
item.description: The White Rock in Hastings is set to host its Christmas panto, Snow White, from Saturday 12 December 2026 to Sunday 3 January 2027. The production features a cast led by Shona McGarty, who plays Snow White, and Matt Terry, who takes the role of Prince Henry.

item.title: Stonehouse View named for Four Courts redevelopment
item.description: Southern Housing has chosen a new name for its proposed major redevelopment of the Four Courts tower blocks in St Leonards. The 1960s social housing scheme, comprising Bevin, Roosevelt, Kennedy, and Churchill Courts, is set to be demolished and rebuilt.

item.title: New cancer support hub to open at Eastbourne DGH
item.description: A new dedicated cancer support hub is set to open at Eastbourne District General Hospital, providing a space for patients and families across East Sussex.

item.title: Hastings Library hosts grief workshops and photo talk in December
item.description: East Sussex Libraries are holding a series of workshops and events about grief throughout December. The programme includes sessions in Hastings, Bexhill, Battle, Rye, and Newhaven, designed for those dealing with personal loss or interested in learning more about bereavement.

item.title: Hastings driver fined for hitting traffic lights
item.description: A man was fined after driving his Mercedes into traffic lights on Old London Road in Hastings. Colin Yeatman, 39, of Hawthorn Road, appeared at Brighton Magistrates' Court. He was found guilty of driving without due care and attention, failing to stop after an accident, and failing to report the incident.

item.title: Christmas Sussex Belle steam train arrives in Hastings tomorrow
item.description: The Christmas Sussex Belle, a historic steam train operated by The Railway Touring Company, is due to visit Hastings tomorrow, November 25. The train will arrive at Hastings station at 3:53pm, hauled by a diesel locomotive from Eastbourne.

item.title: Hastings Old Town traders to hold late-night Christmas shopping event
item.description: Hastings Old Town traders are inviting residents to a late-night Christmas shopping event on Thursday, 3 December. The shops will remain open until 8pm.

item.title: Update: Surviving Christmas cuts hamper numbers to 800 as costs rise
item.description: Surviving Christmas has confirmed it will reduce the number of festive hampers distributed to 800 this year, down from over 1,000 last year, due to rising food costs. The charity said the total cost for food has remained the same, meaning real-term costs have increased by about 45 per cent. It added that the project will still go ahead, with volunteers starting to pack hampers on December 14.

item.title: Update: Police secure closure order for Hastings property
item.description: Police have confirmed the closure order for a flat in St James House, Elphinstone Road, came into effect on 19 November 2026. The order remains in place for three months, restricting access to authorised persons only.

item.title: Hastings United lose 2-0 to Broadbridge Heath in Sussex derby
item.description: Broadbridge Heath took the latest Sussex derby honours by beating Hastings United 2-0 and moving into the Isthmian South East play-off places. The victory saw Broadbridge Heath move into one of the play-off places in seventh – just one point behind Hastings United.

item.title: Surviving Christmas cuts hamper numbers to 800 as costs rise
item.description: Hastings charity Surviving Christmas has reduced the number of festive food hampers it distributes this year, citing the impact of rising costs.

item.title: On this day, 1937: Hastings by-election: Conservative candidate wins seat
item.description: On this day in 1937, the Hastings by-election was held. The contest resulted in a victory for the Conservative candidate, Maurice Hely-Hutchinson.

item.title: Hastings East Sussex Football League teams play out cup thrillers
item.description: Teams in the Macron Sports Hub Hastings East Sussex Football League enjoyed an action-packed weekend as the ESFL Challenge Cup took centre stage. With most clubs involved in cup competition, there was plenty of excitement as teams battled for places in the next round.

item.title: Hastings Rowing Club names new chair and celebrates 2026 awards
item.description: Hastings Rowing Club has marked the end of a successful year at its annual general meeting and awards night. The event brought together members to recognise the contributions of rowers, coaches, and volunteers throughout 2026.

item.title: Penny Pincher's Christmas Carol returns to White Rock Hotel
item.description: A local Christmas comedy tradition is back in Hastings for its ninth year. Penny Pincher’s Christmas Carol, performed by local theatre duo Kate Tym and John Knowles, returns to the White Rock Hotel this December.

item.title: Bexhill unit gets first portable ultrasound in trust
item.description: The Bexhill Irvine Unit has received the trust’s first SonoSite MT Ultrasound System. East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust says the new equipment supports specialist rehabilitation and injection services for patients with complex needs.

item.title: Council leader joins Active Hastings for 20th anniversary
item.description: Councillor Glenn Haffenden, leader of Hastings Borough Council, is visiting Active Hastings sessions to mark the organisation's 20th anniversary. The council leader, who is also the lead councillor for sport and leisure, will meet participants at various venues across the town to hear about the impact of the activities on their health and wellbeing.

item.title: Bohemia Christmas: Free evening of shopping, music and crafts in St Leonards
item.description: A free community celebration is set for the Bohemia area of St Leonards on Thursday 3 December. From 4pm to 7pm, residents can enjoy late-night shopping, live music, Santa, and drop-in craft workshops.

item.title: Update: Hastings council seeks researchers to measure creative industries' economic impact
item.description: Hastings Council has confirmed it is seeking consultants to deliver a detailed assessment of the creative and cultural industries' economic impact, according to The Argus. Proposals for the study must be submitted by 5pm on Thursday, December 31.

item.title: Update: Hastings Pier owner faces fraud trial in Brighton
item.description: Lewes Crown Court, sitting at Brighton, has heard that Sheikh Abid Gulzar, 81, and co-defendant Manasdeep Singh are charged with ten counts of fraud over £160,000 in unpaid water bills at three Eastbourne hotels. Both men deny the charges, which relate to a period since 2018 during which only one payment of £176 was made.

item.title: Jud Charlton performs one-man Christmas Carol in St Leonards
item.description: Actor Jud Charlton is set to perform a one-man adaptation of Charles Dickens’s A Christmas Carol at the Old Church in St Leonards. The production runs from 8 to 17 December, with two shows daily: a matinee for local schools and an evening performance for families.

item.title: Crowhurst Park Lodges wins regional guest satisfaction award
item.description: Crowhurst Park Lodges in Battle has been named the Relax & Explore Small Park destination in the South of England. The holiday park received the honour at Hoseasons’ 21st annual Diamond Awards, which celebrate UK holiday parks and lodge resorts rated highest by guests during the 2026 season.

item.title: Hastings Arts Forum opens Made for Giving popup shop
item.description: A popup shop called Made for Giving opens at the Hastings Arts Forum in Marine Court on Wednesday 25 November. The exhibition features original gifts from 20 local artists, makers, and designers, including paintings, ceramics, textiles, and jewellery.

item.title: Marianne North Centre hosts Victorian orchid talk in Hastings
item.description: The Marianne North Centre is hosting a talk and Q&A session with author Professor Sarah Bilston on Sunday 6 December.

item.title: On this day, 1867: No 1 Battery raised at St Leonards in 1867
item.description: No 1 Battery at St Leonards was originally designated as the 7th Cinque Ports Artillery Volunteer Corps and was raised on 23 November 1867. The unit formed part of the broader Volunteer Movement that emerged following an invasion scare in 1859. This enthusiasm led to the creation of many part-time units, including coastal artillery corps along the Kent and Sussex coast, which were later brought together to form the 1st Cinque Ports Artillery Volunteers at Dover in September 1862.

item.title: Bexhill United clear Midhurst and Easebourne 5-1, move to sixth
item.description: Bexhill United ran out comfortable winners at Polegrove on Saturday, beating Midhurst and Easebourne 5-1 in the latest of a long run of fixtures at the ground that has seen the Pirates climb steadily up the table.

item.title: Update: Hastings Cabinet to discuss fee freeze and heritage funding on 9 November
item.description: The Hastings Borough Council cabinet met on 9 November, and the decisions from that meeting are now recorded. The cabinet recommended the proposed 2027/28 fees and charges on existing services, to be implemented from 1 April 2027, to Full Council, and approved the Age Friendly Hastings strategy, action plan and evaluation framework. It also noted the successful securing of external funding totalling approximately £2.12 million for heritage, leisure and regeneration projects across Hastings.

item.title: Amuse Bouche brings comedy and writing day to Hastings
item.description: Four performers are turning the Downstairs Bar at the White Rock Hotel into a day of comedy and creative writing on the Hastings seafront.

item.title: Hastings man Harun Yildiz jailed for eight years for rape
item.description: A man from Hastings has been jailed for raping a woman, police said.

item.title: Simpler disability allowance set for East Sussex care users
item.description: People in East Sussex who pay towards adult social care will get a simpler way to claim support for disability-related costs, the county council has approved.

item.title: Quit-smoking support brought to Conquest emergency department
item.description: Smokers in Conquest Hospital's emergency department can now get support to quit while they are in hospital.

item.title: Political accountability: County cabinet decisions on care payments and highway policy
item.description: The most significant items for the area this week were decisions published by the county council's lead cabinet members. At the Lead Member for Adult Social Care and Health meeting on Thursday 19 November at 2.00 pm, three decisions were published: the net to gross residential and nursing provider payments business case, the extension of the Integrated Health and Wellbeing Service contract, and proposed changes to Disability Related Expenditure. Area councillor Mark Estcourt was present. Councillor Johnny Denis (Green Party) declared a personal interest as the Lewes District Council cabinet member for community wellbeing, arts, culture, tourism and leisure, and did not consider it to be prejudicial.

item.title: Political accountability: Hastings and Rye MP takes part in every vote of the week
item.description: This week's official record for the MP for Hastings and Rye shows a week of routine votes and written answers, with no item relating to the constituency. Helena Dollimore, the Labour (Co-operative) MP for Hastings and Rye, took part in all ten recorded votes in the Commons.

item.title: Political accountability: Bexhill and Battle MP raises Beckley school PE funding
item.description: The most local item of the week was a Topical Question on Monday about physical education funding at a school in the constituency. Dr Kieran Mullan, the Conservative MP for Bexhill and Battle, said that teachers at Beckley Church of England primary school, as well as parents of pupils, had contacted him about the impact of the Government's reforms to the way physical education is funded in schools on the school's provision, in which there had been a massive drop. He asked the Minister whether she would agree to meet him to discuss what is happening in Beckley and at other schools.

item.title: Political accountability: Hastings Museum Committee meets, minutes not yet published
item.description: The Museum Committee met on Monday 16 November; no minutes are published yet, so no decisions are on the record. An officers' report to the committee said 37,510 people visited the museum in 2025/26 and recommended that the report be accepted and approval recommended to Cabinet.

item.title: Political accountability: Rother licensing panel considers Battle premises licence
item.description: The main local item this week came from the Licensing and General Purposes Committee's General Licensing Panel on Monday 16 November at 10.00 am, whose minutes have been published. The panel appointed Councillor Biggs as chair and considered the report on an application for a premises licence at Battle Abbey School Boarding House, Whatlington Road, Battle. The application covers regulated entertainment, late night refreshment and alcohol sales indoors and outdoors within the premises, Monday to Sunday, 12.00 to 00.30.

item.title: On this day, 1834: Coastguard boat and six crew lost in 1834 rescue attempt
item.description: On 20 November 1834, a Coastguard boat and her six crew were lost whilst attempting to rescue the crew of the collier Good Intent. This tragedy occurred just four years after the French lugger La Constance was driven ashore at Fairlight in 1830, an event that had previously seen two coastguard officers awarded RNIPLS Gold Medals for their rescue efforts in heavy snow and violent seas.

item.title: County council protects payments to Ukrainian family hosts
item.description: East Sussex County Council has stepped in to protect payments to families hosting Ukrainian refugees after the government said the 'thank you' payment would fall from £350 to £100 a month from January 2027.

item.title: County secures £2.9m in road maintenance funding after transparency report
item.description: East Sussex County Council has secured £2.9 million of incentive funding from the Department for Transport for road maintenance after publishing its Highway Maintenance Transparency Report.

item.title: Bexhill pedestrian safety improved with relocated Sea Road zebra crossing
item.description: A zebra crossing in Bexhill has been moved and widened after work to improve pedestrian safety on Sea Road was completed, the county council has confirmed.

item.title: Rother residents asked for views on waste and recycling collections
item.description: Residents across Rother are being asked for their views on the district's waste and recycling collections, Rother District Council has said.

item.title: Hastings charity secretary speaks out for mothers separated from their children
item.description: A Hastings-based charity secretary has talked about the mothers living apart from their children, who still feel judged, she says.

item.title: Hastings Pier owner faces fraud trial in Brighton
item.description: A trial by jury has opened for the owner of Hastings Pier over allegations of fraud, a court heard.

item.title: Hastings water supply under pressure as reservoir stands at 41 per cent
item.description: Hastings households are being told the area's water supply is running well below normal levels, and that winter rain is now needed to top up reservoirs, rivers and groundwater.

item.title: Hastings women take to seafront to support 'Lift the Curfew' campaign
item.description: More than 30 women took to the Hastings seafront on a Wednesday evening at the end of October, torches and hi-vis in hand, to back a national campaign on women's safety when exercising outdoors in the dark.

item.title: On this day, 1997: Michael Foster makes his maiden speech in Parliament
item.description: Michael Foster made his maiden speech on 21 November 1997. He had won the Hastings and Rye seat at the 1997 General Election, where he became the second least expected Labour MP in the landslide. In that election, he defeated the new sitting Conservative MP, Jacqui Lait, by 2,560 votes. Foster served as the Member of Parliament for Hastings and Rye from 1997 to 2010. He was a British lawyer and Labour politician who also served in government as a Minister for Equalities from 2009 to 2010. Foster was born in Hastings, Sussex, and attended the local Hastings Secondary School for Boys and the Hastings Grammar School. He later attended the University of Leicester, where he received a Master of Laws degree. He was admitted as a solicitor in 1980 and worked as a partner of Fynmores Solicitors in Bexhill-on-Sea, specialising in employment law, until 1998.

item.title: Update: Bird deaths spark campaign to remove netting in Hastings and Rother
item.description: East Sussex County Council has confirmed all netting will be wholly removed from Hastings Library once a suitable contractor is found, after a senior council officer wrote to the campaign group apologising for the deaths of the trapped birds. At least nine pigeons were found dead at the four-storey library last month; one surviving pigeon, named Hat-trick, was rescued with the help of Bexhill crane business Coussens and taken into care at RSPCA Mallydams Wood. The group is also pressing B&Q at Ravenside, Bexhill, and the managers of Friston House and Waverley Court in St Leonards to remove their netting.

item.title: Update: Fire-hit St Leonards convent site goes to auction at £1.7m
item.description: The convent's sale will go ahead at auction on 16 December after a Hastings Borough Council panel rejected Save The Convent's application to register the site as an Asset of Community Value, on the grounds that it had formerly been used as a language school. The 11.7 acre site in Magdalen Road is expected to sell at a guide price of £1.7m, in line with its local plan allocation for up to 200 new homes with heritage protection for its Grade II and II* listed buildings.

item.title: More than £20,000 of illegal tobacco seized from East Sussex shops
item.description: More than £20,000 of illegal tobacco has been seized from shops across East Sussex in a major operation to tackle money laundering.

item.title: Battle resident wins £100 of high street vouchers in Solar Town draw
item.description: A Battle resident has won £100 worth of vouchers to spend at independent shops in the town after winning the first prize draw for Battle Solar Town's community solar survey.

item.title: Volunteers invited to care for Rother's micro woods during Tree Week
item.description: Residents are being invited to help look after three community micro woods across Rother during National Tree Week, which runs from 21 to 29 November.

item.title: Metal Christmas tree returns to Hastings town centre
item.description: The illuminated metal Christmas tree has returned to Hastings town centre for a second year, and with it the debate has returned.

item.title: Christmas parking concessions in Battle, Bexhill, Rye and Little Common
item.description: Rother District Council has published its Christmas parking concessions, with charges suspended in a selection of off-street car parks across Battle, Bexhill, Little Common and Rye from late November through December.

item.title: Smudger's Charity Golf Day raises over £7,500 for two local causes
item.description: The 18th Smudger's Charity Golf Day has raised more than £7,500, taking the total raised since the charity launched to more than £110,000, the Hastings Observer reports.

item.title: Planning roundup: new houses, surgery flats and games area among latest applications
item.description: Proposals for four new houses, the conversion of a former GP surgery into flats and a new outdoor sports facility are among the latest planning applications submitted to Hastings Borough Council, the Hastings Observer reports.

item.title: Refugee resettlement project reports 264 moved into work or education
item.description: Hastings Borough Council's Resettlement Employability Project has supported more than 384 people since launching in 2023, with 264 participants moving into employment or education, the council said. That includes 56 people so far this year.

item.title: Hastings council seeks researchers to measure creative industries' economic impact
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has issued a call out to consultants and research teams to undertake a study of what the creative and cultural industries bring to the town's economy.

item.title: UK Disability History Month begins in Hastings
item.description: UK Disability History Month has begun, running until Saturday 19 December, Hastings Borough Council has said. The month celebrates the achievements and contributions of disabled people and encourages reflection on how to create a more inclusive society.

item.title: Battle Town Council marks Remembrance Day and sets festive dates
item.description: Around 150 people gathered on the Battle Abbey Apron for the town's Remembrance Day ceremony, Battle Town Council said. Pupils from Battle & Langton CE Primary School, Claverham Community College and Netherfield CE Primary School gave readings, the Battle Abbey School Choir performed, and the Battle Bonfire Boyes fired the maroon to mark the two-minute silence.

item.title: On this day, 1928: Funerals held for the crew of the Mary Stanford lifeboat
item.description: On Tuesday 20 November 1928, five days after the RNLI lifeboat Mary Stanford capsized and the entire crew of 17 was lost, the town of Rye gathered for the funerals of fifteen of the men, buried in a communal grave.

item.title: Green Automotive Centre of Excellence opens at Ore Valley campus
item.description: A new Green Automotive Centre of Excellence has opened at East Sussex College Group's Ore Valley campus in Hastings.

item.title: Bexhill councillor raises pedestrian safety concerns over 146 homes plan
item.description: A Bexhill councillor has raised concerns over pedestrian safety as part of proposals to build 146 new homes on land off Spindlewood Drive in Little Common.

item.title: Hastings veteran to walk 40 miles for two local charities
item.description: John Holland-Hobbs from Hastings will walk 40 miles in 12 hours on Saturday 28 November to raise funds for the East Sussex Veterans Hub and the Hastings and Rother Ukrainian Branch.

item.title: Christmas Tree Festival returns to St Clements Church
item.description: St Clements Church in Hastings Old Town is holding its popular Christmas Tree Festival from Saturday 28 November.
